ca_texas_canyon.blurb: Texas Canyon lies in the Angeles National Forest hills of northwest Los Angeles County, between Santa Clarita and Agua Dulce. Big domes, standalone formations and boulders of coarse conglomerate hold almost all of the climbing, which is overwhelmingly bolted sport, with a few trad lines, top ropes and boulder problems mixed in. Grades cluster from 5.10 to 5.12, with a decent supply of 5.7 to 5.9 routes and a handful of harder ones. The stone is pocketed and knobby, and the terrain swings from gentle slab to steep overhangs and caves, with some formations around 200 feet tall. The rock is brittle, so holds can snap, and it stays damp for days after rain. Most of the year works, apart from the hottest and coldest days. Busy sub-areas include the First Corridor, Tower of Babel and the Caves on the Elephant Head.

co_keystone_a_k_a_montezuma.blurb: Keystone, also called Montezuma, sits about 9,400 feet up in Colorado's Front Range, a few miles from Keystone town on the southern slopes of Porcupine Peak. The rock is solid alpine granite, and the climbing is a blend of bolted sport routes, trad cracks, top ropes and a big boulder field. Sport and trad grades mostly run from 5.9 to 5.11 with a good number of 5.12s, while the bouldering reaches from easy V0 problems into the higher V grades, with plenty in the middle. The crags face south but pick up shade through part of the day, and the elevation makes this a cooler summer choice than the Denver-area cliffs. Main objectives include the Hummingbird Boulders, Haus Rock and Morning Glory Wall.

az_stewart_pocket.blurb: Stewart Pocket is a scenic basin at roughly 5,000 feet, a couple of miles southeast of Payson in central Arizona. Granite domes, towers, boulders and ridges ring the basin, and the rock is mostly solid granite. Trad climbing leads the way, with a good helping of sport, some bouldering and a little aid. Most routes fall between 5.7 and 5.11, with 5.10 the most common grade and only a few at 5.12. The place is still lightly developed, so it feels quiet and open-ended, set in pinyon and juniper woodland. Larger formations include Hippy Dome, Stewart Peak and Foreplay Wall, and The Joint is the biggest sport cluster. Hiking and mountain biking also draw people to the neighbouring hills.

bc_elbow_lake_bouldering.blurb: Elbow Lake Bouldering is a lakeside boulder zone east of Mission in the Fraser Valley, on a hillside beneath a tall granite wall. Every climb here is a boulder problem, with well over a hundred in total. Grades run from V0 up to V10, but the bulk sit between V0 and V4, so there is plenty for newer boulderers alongside a thinner tail of hard lines. Upper Slide holds the most problems, followed by the Sasquatch Boulders and Lower Slide. The setting is sunny and exposed, and it can get very hot in summer, though the boulders dry quickly after rain and the lake is handy for cooling off. The cliff above the lake adds roughly fifty bolted and trad routes.

ab_echo_canyon.blurb: Echo Canyon is a hard sport-climbing canyon above Canmore in Alberta's Bow Valley, reached by a trail that climbs a dry creek bed. Every route is bolted. Nearly all fall between 5.11 and 5.13, with only a thin scattering of 5.10 and a couple of 5.14s, so it suits climbers who already lead at a solid level. Lines are both long and short, with technical, crimpy, pumpy and juggy styles, and the rock is praised for its quality. The Lookout and Coliseum hold most of the routes, with the Hideaway a smaller cluster. Fall is considered the best season, as the weaker sun keeps the rock warm. The Lookout and Hideaway get strong sun and can be crowded on weekends.
